57762.requiredPriorKnowledge: There are no formal entry requirements, but a basic knowledge of the history and material culture of the Ancient World and its cultures is expected. Recommended literature in case of deficiencies: (Ancient Middle-East) - Blois, L. de & R.J. van der Spek, 2019, An Introduction to the Ancient World , 3rd edition, London/New York. Chapters 1-7 (excluding Egypt) (Greek world) - Barringer, J.M. 2015, The Art and Archaeology of Ancient Greece , Cambridge. Chapters 3-4. (Roman world) Rüpke, J., 2007. Religion of the Romans , Cambridge/Malden MA. Chapters 7-8.

57940.name: Ancient Philosophy
57940.recommendedPriorKnowledge: Some prior knowledge of Greco-Roman antiquity is highly recommended, but not required.

58082.name: Cultural Contact: East and West
58082.requiredPriorKnowledge: For this course knowledge of ancient history is required. Students must combine this course with A Cultural History of the Ancient World 1: The Near East and the Greek world or have followed another introductory course relating to Ancient History.

58128.name: Cultural Contact: Mediterranean Connections
58128.entryRequirements: A Cultural History of the Ancient World 1: The Near East and the Greek world and A Cultural History of the Ancient World 2: The Hellenistic world, Italy and Rome (or similar introductory courses) should have been completed.
58128.recommendedPriorKnowledge: This course on the intermediate level builds on several of the beginners’ classes from the BA in Ancient Studies. It assumes basic knowledge of the Ancient World, as offered in the courses A Cultural History of the Ancient World 1: The Near East and the Greek world and A Cultural History of the Ancient World 2: The Hellenistic world, Italy and Rome and further develops the topic of cultural contact, which is started in the first-year module Cultural Contact: East and West . Unlike those first-year modules, this is not a survey course offering an overview of facts about connections in the ancient Mediterranean and requires more independent work.

findings: The current joint OER 10.2 and 11.3–11.6 confirm Ancient History as first-listed English specialisation. The generic target does not prescribe a route. This broad historical option is selected before UCR implementation, rather than a language or material-method specialisation. Eight first-year core courses plus Classical Mythology and Seminar Ancient History total sixty EC. Seven second-year core courses and the three history courses total sixty. Lieux de memoire, two advanced specialisation courses, thirty open EC and the twelve-credit thesis total sixty. Mutually exclusive specialisations in the guide group totals are not added together.

Article 11.4 permits the two named orientation choices. The VU 2026 seminar page explicitly identifies BA1 Ancient Studies students and prior CHAW1/2. These are taken before the period-five seminar. The VU descriptions redirected by UvA confirm Near Eastern history, politics and international relations, and world heritage. The Near Eastern route alone requires prior Akkadian and additional translation work; Ancient History does not. Roman Decline requires enrolment in Ancient History, satisfied here.

Joint OER 9.1 requires positive BSA for post-propaedeutic study and all first- and second-year courses before starting the thesis. Article 14.1 sets BSA at forty-eight first-year EC. Mediterranean Connections requires both cultural-history surveys; East and West combines with the first survey. The individual interdisciplinary thesis includes its colloquium. The literacy diagnostic, orientation and tutoring carry no credit. Article 11.7 lists practical exercises and requires eighty-five percent participation.

World Heritage is compulsory for Ancient History under joint OER 11.6. The VU entry refers generically to MKDA regulations. MKDA 9.1 describes progression into years of that programme; it does not name a course-specific prerequisite. The joint Ancient Studies rules govern this route and prescribe the course after its own foundation. No unrelated MKDA specialisation or English course is imposed on Ancient Studies students. Both first years are completed before the third-year heritage course.

Article 12.1 controls electives: outside the two joint institutions needs approval, placements may occupy at most twelve of the thirty EC, normally at most twelve EC is introductory and at least twenty-four EC is outside the programme, with specified exceptions. The online choice page is stricter about outside-UvA approval; the adopted joint rule controls. Open space is not instantiated and no placement is required.
